```bash
MODEL=REPLACE_WITH_MODEL_CONFIG_FILENAME_STEM
cd "$CAMPAIGN"
./validate-campaign.sh
./launch-campaign.sh --submit --model "$MODEL"
```

Use `--suite nonagentic`, `--suite agentic`, or `--suite terminal-bench` for a complete suite
subset. Use repeatable `--evalchemy NAME` or `--harbor NAME` selectors for a named recovery. AIME24,
OlympiadBench, and GPQA Diamond perform their repeated sampling inside one launch using the shared
seeded-repeat implementation; AIME24 is not launched ten times. Omitting `--submit` is a dry run.

### Three-benchmark reproduction check

For a release-level smoke reproduction, use model-config stem `Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` and these
fixed benchmarks: GSM8K 0-shot (`0.908`), MATH500 (`0.984`), and DS-1000 (`0.270`). Launch each
benchmark separately with the Marin command above:

```bash
MODEL=Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
./launch-campaign.sh --submit --wait --limit 50 --suite nonagentic --model "$MODEL" --evalchemy gsm8k-0shot
./launch-campaign.sh --submit --wait --limit 50 --suite nonagentic --model "$MODEL" --evalchemy math500
./launch-campaign.sh --submit --wait --limit 50 --suite agentic --model "$MODEL" --harbor ds-1000-local
```

Each launch prints a run ID such as
`20260929-150059-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-piqa-ef1c`. After the waiting command exits, inspect that
run's durable record with the following command. It prints the scoreable-trial count followed by
the primary score; repeat it with the run ID from each launch.

```bash
RUN_ID=REPLACE_WITH_PRINTED_RUN_ID
RECORDS_PREFIX=s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals
bash -lc '
  source ./common.sh
  resolve_coreweave_credentials
  uv run --project "$MARIN_DIR" fsutil cat --raw \
    "'$RECORDS_PREFIX'/'$RUN_ID'/record.json"
' | python3 -c '
import json, sys
record = json.load(sys.stdin)
status = record["status"]
if status != "completed":
    error = record.get("error")
    raise SystemExit(f"run did not complete: {status}: {error}")
coverage = next(iter(record["coverage"].values()))
metrics = next(iter(record["canonical_metrics"].values()))
score = next(value for name, value in metrics.items() if not name.endswith("_stderr"))
print(coverage["n_scored"], score)
'
```

After at least 50 scoreable trials, compare their mean with the corresponding reported score. For this
provisional smoke check, parity means an absolute difference no greater than `0.146`. This is the
worst-case 95% normal half-width for 50 independent `[0, 1]` trial rewards,
`1.96 × 0.5 / sqrt(50)`, expanded by `1 / sqrt(0.9)` for the policy's infrastructure tolerance.
This gate is intentionally a smoke reproduction, not a replacement for the full-run confidence
intervals or release result.

```bash
    model_args+=",chat_template_kwargs={\"$thinking_key\":$thinking_value}"
  fi
  uv run eval \
    --model local-chat-completions \
    --model_args "$model_args" \
    --tasks "$task_name" \
    --num_fewshot "$num_fewshot" \
    "${extra[@]}" \
    --output_path "results/evalchemy/$output_name" \
    "$@"
}
```

## Run resumption

Resume an interrupted Harbor run only when its model, checked-out repository revision, runtime
limit, and dataset state are unchanged. Read the original run ID and effective configuration from
its durable `record.json`. Use the model and Harbor config from the same Marin commit, then add the
original run ID:

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$CAMPAIGN/model-configs/<model-config>.yaml" \
  --harbor-config "$STAGED_HARBOR_DIR/<harbor-config>.yaml" \
  --resume-run-id <original-run-id>
```

The durable `<records-prefix>/<original-run-id>/results/harbor_jobs/` tree must remain accessible.
Harbor preserves completed scored trials and reruns missing attempts and exceptions in its pinned
resume taxonomy. Use a clean replacement when model, policy, pins, limits, records prefix, or
dataset state changed, or when the unscored error is outside that taxonomy. Never delete a trial
directory to force recovery.

## Baseline-specific launch settings

The YAML files under
`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/model-configs/` are authoritative for checkpoint and tokenizer
revisions, serving context, GPU count, tensor and data parallelism, reasoning parser, tool parser,
sampling overrides, and Pi `thinking_format`. Use the matching file unchanged. Pi uses
`qwen-chat-template` for Qwen3.6 and Qwen3-Next and `chat-template` for the other models.

## Updating codebase pins

Use the newest campaign pin for each codebase across the full release, assuming forward
compatibility with earlier score-producing runs. If a pin change causes an observed result
regression, stop launches, fix or revert the change, and issue a new policy version when the
evaluation behavior intentionally changes. Preserve the original run's exact pins in its immutable
config snapshot even after the release-wide pins advance.

## Standards for presenting Marin evals

* Display score cells in the standard tracker and any tournament-only tracker to three significant digits. Apply the same convention to a tracker formed from their union. The linked durable run records retain unrounded scores. Tournament and figure analyses recover full-precision task aggregates from that durable evidence; tracker values are presentation-only.
* Select the release Snowball checkpoint by the uncertainty-aware paired tournament defined in “How do we choose which model to release?” Release figures include only the selected checkpoint, not the other Snowball candidates. The Snowball candidate family includes Grug 67B A2B checkpoints as well as checkpoints named Snowball. For each benchmark, plot the selected Snowball checkpoint and every non-Snowball baseline with an available score and total-training-FLOP estimate. Performance is on the y-axis and total training FLOPs are on a logarithmic x-axis. A baseline with an incomplete suite may appear in the scatterplots for its completed benchmarks, but it is excluded from cross-benchmark critical-difference analysis unless it has the full common benchmark panel.
* Produce uncertainty-aware normalized critical-difference diagrams with and without a FLOP control. Normalize scores within each benchmark across the complete-panel cohort. Estimate each score's task-level sample SEM from the scored trial rewards, then multiply the SEM by `1 / sqrt(0.9)` to account conservatively for the policy's 10% infrastructure-failure tolerance. With a fixed random seed, draw 100,000 score panels from independent normal sampling distributions centered on the reported scores and clipped to the metric's `[0, 1]` range. Rank models within every benchmark for each draw, using average ranks for ties, and report mean ranks with simultaneous 95% bands based on the draw-wise maximum absolute rank deviation. Report the Nemenyi critical difference at `alpha = 0.05`; it depends on the number of models and benchmarks, while score uncertainty affects the simulated rank distribution and its simultaneous bands.
* For the FLOP-controlled diagram, regress the draw's benchmark-normalized scores on `log10(total training FLOPs)` with one common linear slope, rank the within-benchmark residuals, and otherwise use the same uncertainty procedure. Treat FLOP estimates as fixed point estimates and disclose that their estimation uncertainty is not propagated. The uncontrolled diagram ranks the sampled normalized scores directly.
* We use a 6ND proxy for pretraining FLOPS, and 6 * max_tokens_per_rollout / max_context_length * n_rollouts * active_params proxy for RL FLOPS; that said, we are the only lab, as of this writing, which releases RL FLOPS, so meaningful comparisons are impossible. From the few labs who release midtraining / SFT information, we derive an unweighted mean percentage of FLOPS devoted to midtraining. We then estimate midtraining FLOPS for other labs using that mean. We estimate total FLOPS as the sum of pretraining FLOPS + (all midtraining / non-RL) FLOPS + (all RL and OPD) FLOPS. For any model which doesn't give sufficient evidence for any of the three stages, use the mean FLOPS over all models in the cohort as the estimated  FLOPS for that stage.
* In a separate standalone table, include all raw scores in XX.y format, with 95% confidence intervals derived from the trial count and the infrastructure error tolerance -- do not leave gaps, use table captions for results that require further context, use the exact same model family in the table as was present in the x-y scatterplot(s)
* Eval results are reportable IFF the eval in question completed with no more than 10% of trials encountering infrastructure errors
* Eval results are reportable IFF they include provenance, in the form of model traces, and where available, verifier traces
* Any eval result that is publicly presented should clearly distinguish whether the benchmarks are in-distribution (part of the dev set), held out, or a mix of the two
* Any eval result that is publicly presented in a major release should report on *all* ID and OOD benchmarks, avoiding cherry picking, substitution, or new evals outside of a formal policy update
* For active development and internal communication, it is fine to define working subsets of the ID benchmarks and report on those in isolation

### Reproduce SOTOPIA-hard length control

SOTOPIA-Hard length control was introduced post-hoc, after the agent traces were generated. For this generation of eval policy, it needs to be run separately. The details on how to do so live here.

The Harbor verifier writes the unadjusted normalized overall reward and
`sotopia_response_characters` for every completed episode. The release score is a cohort
statistic, so it must be regenerated across all compared models rather than copied from one
Harbor run's aggregate. From the pinned Marin checkout, with CoreWeave S3 read credentials and
the campaign tracker available locally, run:

```bash
TRACKER=/absolute/path/to/TRACKER.md
OUTPUT_DIR=/absolute/path/to/artifacts/sotopia-length-controlled-overall
uv run python experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/analysis/sotopia_length_control/rank.py \
  --tracker "$TRACKER" --output-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR"
```

The tool reads the seven dimension scores and transcripts from each sealed SOTOPIA-hard archive,
measures only the evaluated agent's emitted characters, and groups cross-validation folds by task.
It writes both raw and length-controlled rankings, plus the tracker SHA-256, every source archive,
the selected regularization strength, and all cross-validation losses. Its counterfactual sets the
response-length difference to zero relative to each task's cohort median. Adding or removing a
model changes that median and requires recomputing the complete cohort. A policy-valid
infrastructure failure retains its configured zero; unscored infrastructure failures are excluded
under the campaign's sealing rule.

The tracker-linked October 15 cohort output is preserved at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/ablations/sotopia-overall-length-controlled-20261015-c5ef5789/`.

### Reproduce the Snowball tournament and critical-difference figures

Use the campaign tracker as a point-in-time input: every numeric cell must contain its durable
S3 result link, either a native `/results` archive or a corrected per-trial replay JSON. The
tournament requires complete observed scores for every Snowball or Grug candidate on its
23-benchmark selection panel; it excludes FinanceBench, PIQA, and TriviaQA. It derives each cell's
full-precision task aggregate and task-level SEM from the durable trial evidence, then expands the
SEM by `1 / sqrt(0.9)`. The three-decimal tracker score is presentation-only. A benchmark is a
win only when `abs(score_a - score_b) > 1.96 * hypot(adjusted_sem_a, adjusted_sem_b)`; otherwise it
is a tie. A win is one vote, a tie half a vote, and each candidate's selection statistic is the
unweighted mean of its paired win rates against the other candidates. Preserve the generated
tracker and recovered-metrics SHA-256 values, and do not combine a tournament selection with
figures generated from a different tracker snapshot.

The analysis tools are in the Marin campaign worktree under
`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/analysis/`, in the
`snowball_tournament/` and `critical_difference/` subdirectories. From the pinned Marin checkout,
with the campaign tracker and output directory available locally, run:

```bash
TRACKER=/absolute/path/to/TRACKER.md
OUTPUT_DIR=/absolute/path/to/artifacts
uv run python experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/analysis/snowball_tournament/pairwise.py \
  --tracker "$TRACKER" --recovered-metrics "$OUTPUT_DIR/recovered-record-metrics.json" \
  --output-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR/snowball-tournament"
uv run python experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/analysis/critical_difference/plot.py \
  --tracker "$TRACKER" --selection "$OUTPUT_DIR/snowball-tournament/snowball_selection.json" \
  --recovered-metrics "$OUTPUT_DIR/recovered-record-metrics.json" \
  --output-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR/critical-difference"
```

Both commands need read access to the scored results in CoreWeave S3; configure the normal
Marin `fsutil` credentials first. It reads canonical `record.json` files for trial counts and
normalized sample rewards for non-binary metrics. If a NUPA record has not been written, the
tool requires its sealed native Evalchemy archive and verifies its coverage and canonical score.
For cells sealed from an interrupted executor,
`recovered-record-metrics.json` supplies the independently aggregated scored-trial count and
reward standard error; retain that audit file with the tracker. The complete-panel cohort is the selected
Snowball plus the non-Snowball models listed in `critical_difference/baseline_flops.csv`; a
benchmark enters the diagrams only if every cohort model has a numeric, linked score. The output
includes every benchmark-level pair outcome, the full paired-win matrix and selection summary,
per-cell sample statistics, FLOP estimates, rank tables, and uncontrolled and FLOP-controlled PNG,
PDF, and SVG figures. Regenerate
both commands after any tracker change. The uncertainty, normalization, FLOP-control, and
critical-difference calculations are defined above; the random seed and draw count are fixed in
the plotting code.

## Future considerations

* We would like to post-train multiple Snowball checkpoints, experimenting with different degrees of compute applied to post-training, to establish trade-off lines / domains
* We would like to think about a "marin model card" that would set minimum standards for true open development
* amd/Instella-MoE-16B-A3B-Think is not runnable currently from our pinned vLLM fork, but we would like to look at this model in the future
* We still weren't able to land a trusted K2 Horizon baseline set of scores yet
* evaluate our baselines on OOD as well as ID
* JudgeArena multilingual, maybe one of those cultural idiom / include benchmarks, restore simpleQA-mini, a long context supplement for MRCR
* Produce a summary of why we think the previously flagged TB2 / TB4 task description overlap are likely not problematic, if they are not
* Find a better instruction following benchmark than IFBench
* Consider a smaller subset of MMLU-Pro and NUPA so they run faster
* Fix the inconsistency in Evalchemy timeout error handling
* In the future, we may deliberately use subsets of very large benchmarks like BFCL and NUPA as training material; in this case, we must mark the full benchmarks as explicitly contaminated, adding a new section to our eval policy
* Properly unify on the co-hosted MiniMax judge
* Consider using a judge panel and requiring all judges to agree on equivalence
* Consider using cruxeval input as well as output
* Drop PIQA as non-discriminating, TriviaQA needs its grader reconsidered
* biomedical knowledge: MedXpertQA or PubMedQA, Clinical reasoning: HealthBench Professional/ Bedside Bench /ASCENT, Biological discovery: Longevity — genetics regression; LAB-Bench cloning / DNA methylation age comparison, Medical coding: MedConceptsQA — ATC Hard/ MedConceptsQA ICD-10 procedures, hard

comments.author: bethehand
comments.body:
Was the unpaired tie rule a deliberate choice? `pairwise.py` treats a benchmark as a tie unless `abs(score difference) > 1.96 * hypot(adjusted SEMs)`, i.e. as if the two models' scores were independent. Both models answer the same tasks, so the SE that matters is that of the per-task difference, and it is usually smaller:
- In the per-sample outputs in [marin-community/grug-67b-a2b-snowball-post-sft-evals](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/grug-67b-a2b-snowball-post-sft-evals) (Grug-67B-A2B SFT and six MoE models from other families; pairs within 15 points), the paired SE is 0.63× the unpaired one on ARC-C, 0.74× on MATH500, 0.77× on BoolQ, 0.78× on WinoGrande, 0.83× on GPQA Diamond and 0.94× on GSM8K (medians).
- On public SWE-bench Verified results it is 0.71× for 467 similar-strength pairs and 0.65× for 10 pairs within one model family (medians), so same-base candidates will likely gain more than the numbers above.

With several samples per task, the task should be the unit. In the same outputs (AIME24, 3 samples per problem), the task-level SE is 1.45–1.60× the per-sample SE for Grug and the three Qwen models, and the gap grows with more samples per task. Yet 71 of the 84 #10199 cells on TBLite, TB2.1, AIME24 and OlympiadBench (3–10 samples per task) compute the SEM per sample. AIME24 also mixes bases: 13 of its 21 cells use n = 30 and the rest n = 300, about 25 vs 8 points of threshold at p ≈ 0.7.

What it could change, scaling every threshold by one factor r (the tournament's per-sample rewards aren't public):
- In [#10199](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10199) and [#10283](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10283), 51% of benchmark comparisons are ties, and about 10% of all comparisons are ties with |d| ≥ 0.71× the threshold.
- [#10283](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10283)'s pick, Smartie step14, holds for every r down to 0.5. [#10199](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10199)'s pick, Campaign3, led Campaign2 by half a point in 460 comparisons; Campaign2 leads outright at every r ≤ 0.96, or r ≤ 0.928 if only the other 19 benchmarks are scaled.
- [#10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) promotes an arm only on a decisive win over plain and expects one policy run to resolve 4–5 points on SWE-bench Verified. In [#10199](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10199) the SWE-bench thresholds between Campaign3 (30.9%) and candidates at 23–32% are 5.8–6.2 points; at r = 0.71, 4.1–4.4.

#9582 and #9519 already use paired bootstraps. If useful, I can rerun these tables on an export of the per-sample rewards. Code and tables: [paired-eval](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/8da9efeb8c451fc564f3cc3e7bafcd972c3e2f7a/paired-eval).

(Side note: in that dataset's samples files, `correct` is true on every GPQA Diamond, AIME24, HumanEval+, MBPP+ and IFEval row, so I rescored GPQA and AIME24 from `extracted`.)

comments.body:
🤖 For the next eval policy version: evaluate serving Marin models (Snowball, Grug) with the `grug` reasoning parser. We should lean towards adopting it, or fix the policy or the parser so that adopting it helps. @chrismc91

**Current state.** None of the #10197 model configs sets a reasoning parser for Snowball or Grug checkpoints, so every one of their cells was served without one. The parser exists ([marin-community/vllm#79](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/79)) and separates `<|start_think|>…<|end_think|>` from the final answer. #9431 used it for the Sept 21 Grug config, and the structure-closure tournament requires it. Baselines are served with their own reasoning parsers, so Marin models are the exception.

**Observed cost.** Without a parser, the model's reasoning is part of the graded text, and vLLM strips the think markers. On CRUXEval, Snowball's reasoning often restates the instruction "surround the answer with [ANSWER] and [/ANSWER] tags". The grader takes the first `[ANSWER]` span, so it grades " and ".
- The Snowball v0.1 T=0.6 re-run had 78 such failures and the original run had 51.
- The two baselines checked (Qwen3.6, Gemma 4) had none.
- With a grader-side fix, the input direction goes from 0.714 to 0.793.
- Details are in the #10283 correction and [this gist](https://gist.github.com/penfever/707865d8595b451c1276112bc3e94069).
- A grader fix is in progress, but other benchmarks that grade the full response may carry the same bias.

**Suggested evaluation for the next version:**
- Re-run the Marin cohort with and without `reasoning_parser: grug` on the benchmarks that grade the full response (Evalchemy chat tasks, IFBench, CRUXEval, MRCR, NUPA), and on the agentic suites that consume `reasoning_content`.
- Report the paired deltas.
- If the parser hurts somewhere, for example where a harness drops `reasoning_content` that it needs, fix that harness or the parser rather than serving without it.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 On the [proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197#issuecomment-6660805264) to serve Marin models with the `grug` parser: we served `Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` and `Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10` twice each, without a reasoning parser and with marin-community/vllm#79's parser. Marin's Evalchemy sent both servers the campaign's requests with matching seeds, and Marin main's graders scored IFBench, CRUXEval, MRCR, NUPA5K-Loose (step 14 only), HumanEval+, MBPP+, GSM8K, TriviaQA and MATH500.

Paired deltas, parser minus no parser, with 95% intervals:
- TriviaQA: +2.32 [1.96, 2.70] on step 14, +0.52 [0.24, 0.80] on Campaign2. Its extractor reads `Answer:` only at the start of a line, and without a parser that line runs on from the reasoning.
- NUPA5K-Loose: +66.32, because main's scorer gives the text served without a parser 0.12 points. Main's Grug configs have sent `skip_special_tokens: false` since #10876, and that state scores within 0.2 points of the parser. Under the scorer behind the tracker's NUPA cells the delta is -0.30 [-1.44, 0.82].
- IFBench on Campaign2: -3.33 [-6.67, -0.33], a sampling difference between the servers.
- Every other interval includes zero.

On the same tokens the parser changes no grade on IFBench, CRUXEval, HumanEval+, MBPP+ or GSM8K, because Evalchemy's default `combine` hands the grader reasoning plus content. CRUXEval's `and` extractions stay at 54 input and 2 output on step 14 (82 and 0 in a temperature 0.6 run). The gains need a grader that reads only the final content, the default that #10927 proposes for canonical tasks. On the same tokens that leaves 2 input extractions on step 14 (11 at temperature 0.6) and adds 7.12 points to step 14's CRUXEval input, 5.49 to HumanEval+ and 2.67 to IFBench. At most 7 replies per benchmark lack final content.

Caveats: one sample per item, identical tokens across servers for only some replies, and no agentic suites.

## 10/05 Micro210 baseline

Evaluation-only entry for the frozen 10/05 model; this does not introduce a new SFT or RL training recipe.

Micro210 is Marin’s mixed reasoning, knowledge, coding and agentic evaluation suite.
This recipe supports 200 distinct tasks across 20 sources (Tau3 excluded), expanded to 440 assignments, including 100 Pi assignments.

## Model and evaluation policy

Model: [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05/tree/ac60d9401820953943f5a56e06f36e13c86b12d6), immutable revision `ac60d9401820953943f5a56e06f36e13c86b12d6`. The three runs evaluate this same model in existing region-local storage, with no additional training.

The runtime separately selects [marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools](https://huggingface.co/marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools/tree/3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09), revision `3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09`, with no explicit template override and thinking enabled. The model’s embedded tokenizer provenance is not the selected runtime tools revision.

Current harness: 16 global Harbor slots (four rollout workers × four), one 8 H100 policy worker (TP1/DP8/EP8, max_num_seqs 8) and an independent 8 H100 M3 judge (TP8). Policy/judge caps are 21,600 s; root cap is 25,200 s. Native Pi 0.87; context 65,536, 16,384 generated tokens per turn, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95. Compilation and CUDA graphs remain enabled. These role budgets are not asserted identical to every historical recipe in this issue.

| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TruthfulQA | `\boxed{A}` | 100 | 70 | 80 | 70 | 20 | 90 |
| GPQA Diamond | `B` | 50 | 56.7 | 56.7 | 43.3 | 33.3 | 66.7 |
| MMLU-Pro | `I don't know.` | 40 | 70 | 70 | 60 | 40 | 90 |
| IFBench | `hello` | 10 | 40 | 40 | 30 | 0 | 40 |

The other ten answer benchmarks score 0 for every reply. The six agentic benchmarks were not run.

- TruthfulQA: the generated-choice prompts list the options in `mc2_targets` order, which starts with a true answer. Option A is true in every task: 10 in Micro210, 41 in Mini840, 817 rows of `truthfulqa/truthful_qa`. A seeded shuffle of each task's options would remove this. The full policy's MC2 likelihood scoring does not depend on order.
- MMLU-Pro: without `answer is (X)` or `Answer: X`, the extractor takes the last standalone capital A-J, so `I don't know.` counts as option I, the key of 4 tasks.
- GPQA Diamond: 5 of the 10 drawn keys are B.
- IFBench: the prepared rows grade it with the `evalchemy` wheel of `runtime-v4`, whose IFBench checkers are byte-identical to `vendor/evalchemy` before #10423. In one of the 10 tasks (key 278, the capitals of European countries north of 45°) a correct reply cannot pass: the checker's list leaves out Kyiv, so the 28 correct capitals score 0 and the 27 without Kyiv score 1.

This does not show that a round guesses. On these 10 tasks, the three benchmarks cannot tell a round from a constant below the floor. They carry 8.7 of Round 3's 41.07 points. Without them, Rounds 1-3, the base and Snowball v0.1 average 49.8, 44.7, 38.1, 13.3 and 40.3%.

Launcher floors rerun with `trivial_replies` on #11222's head over a TaskSpec corpus of a benchmark's prepared tasks. The TruthfulQA count needs only the dataset (`uv run --with pyarrow --with huggingface_hub python check.py`):

```python
import base64, json
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

path = hf_hub_download("open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210", "data/validation.parquet", repo_type="dataset",
                       revision="4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819")
labels = []
for row in pq.read_table(path).to_pylist():
    if row["benchmark"] == "truthfulqa":
        files = json.loads(row["task_spec"])["resources"]["verifier"]
        config = json.loads(base64.b64decode(next(f for f in files if f["path"] == "config.json")["source"]["content_base64"]))
        labels.append(config["spec"]["doc"]["mc2_targets"]["labels"][0])
print(f"option A is true in {sum(labels)} of {len(labels)} TruthfulQA tasks")
```

comments.body: @weaverbot OOC, can you give a short description of your best guess for why the RL results for Mochi are lackluster here? My best guess is that the data mix that improves Snowball is already basically handled by Mochi, so RL just churns? Or is it more subtle?

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/jqs797xf

- 🟢 `Nov 24 17:03Z` Answered Mochi RL question on #11337: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7138614864

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 My best guess is that Mochi’s strong SFT starting point leaves less easy gain from this RL pool, but the result looks like more than harmless churn. Under the same frozen Micro210 policy, Mochi fell from 59.7% SFT to 52.9% at RL step 22 (413 vs 428 scored attempts, so this is not a paired estimate). The known CRUXEval grader defect exaggerates the benchmark-mean drop; excluding that cell still leaves 68.3% → 62.2% across the other 18 benchmarks ([sealed scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7120866787)).

Training reward rose while the fixed holdout was roughly flat or down versus pre-RL ([curves](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12119); scored subsets vary), consistent with optimizing the sampled reward without broad transfer. Mochi also used a different RL mix/sampler and MuonH at 1e-5; step 22 was the **final-checkpoint fallback** because no holdout evaluation met the coverage gate. So I would suspect limited headroom *plus* recipe/selection effects, rather than data redundancy alone. We cannot apportion those yet, and Snowball round 1 used a different RL recipe and eval policy ([comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12201)). The useful next checks are paired holdout comparisons, the diagnostic earlier checkpoint, and the planned optimizer/LR ablation ([#12103](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12103)).

comments.body:
🤖 **BixBench re-scored offline on every sealed 2026.11.23 Micro210 row** — coverage repair for the pass@1 table (#10197)

**Cause.** Every `bixbench-pi` trial in these rows ended `"Harbor trial has no verifier score"`: the Harbor trial-config rebuild round-tripped the verifier env through a redacting serializer, which turned the judge-relay placeholder `OPENAI_API_KEY="EMPTY"` into the literal `"****"`, and Harbor's task-environment boundary rejected that literal before the verifier ran (`ValueError: Provider credentials must remain on the host; use a Shellbox model relay: OPENAI_API_KEY`). So the one judge-required Harbor row produced `n_scored 0` everywhere and silently dropped out of pass@1. Fixed by 4fd392c07a (`[skyrl] Keep the projected verifier credentials through the Harbor trial rebuild`); a fresh bixbench-only run on the fix scores 3/10 with real judge verdicts.

**Method (no GPU re-runs).** The archived per-trial trajectories are complete, so each trial's proposed answer was extracted with the package's own `<answer>` rule and graded offline with the frozen judge binding (`micro210_inputs.bixbench_judge_resources`: Together `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, strict `binary_score` schema, max_tokens 1024, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, reasoning_effort low — the same client the prepared tasks run in-container). 52 answered trials judged, 0 judge failures; trials with no answer in the trajectory failed closed to 0 (#10197: agent failures score 0, only genuine infra errors are excluded). Each row's revised aggregate was published as a NEW artifact next to the sealed record (`<run>/aggregate-bixbench-v2.jsonl`), and each row got a revised EvalDash record as a new version (`<run>-bixbench-v2`); nothing sealed was overwritten.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
A model reply with malformed tool-call arguments stops the whole evaluation run at grading time, not just its own attempt. In an 8-task SWE-bench-Science run with mini-swe-agent on Daytona, Nemotron 3.5 Super returned a `bash` tool call whose `arguments` JSON was cut off mid-string. When that attempt was graded, the worker raised and ended the run after 2 minutes: 5 attempts had been recorded and the other 3, still running, were lost.

```
rolloutengine/grading.py:83  GradingAttempt(chat_conversation(list(messages)), ...)
taskcompendium/chat.py:72    ChatAssistantMessage.model_validate(message)
ValidationError: tool_calls.0.function.arguments
  Value error, Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 12 (char 11)
```

`_grade_rollout` builds a `GradingAttempt` from the transcript for every grader, including script graders that grade the task machine and never read the conversation. `assistant_message` deliberately rejects invalid JSON arguments at this boundary, so one malformed reply raises a `ValidationError`. `_score_rollout` (`lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py`) treats any error outside `RETRYABLE_ERRORS` as permanent and re-raises it after saving the attempt, and the worker's task group then cancels every other attempt. The trigger is model output, which a weaker or truncated model produces often, so full runs on smaller models will hit it.

Two possible directions. The narrow one: record an attempt whose transcript cannot be validated as a failed submission scored 0, the same outcome as other malformed model output, and keep grading the rest of the run. The broader one: have the worker record any unexpected exception raised while grading as that attempt's infrastructure failure instead of ending the run; #12268 fixed one instance of the same pattern, a Daytona grader machine that vanished while starting.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
### Summary
The SWE-bench-style shared graders (the taskcompendium log parsers behind the SWE_REBENCH profile) record reward 0.0 for rows whose full test suites PASS in an identical environment. The F2P/P2P parse fails to match the config's test ids against the suite output, so fully-passing suites score 0.0.

### Evidence (SWE-rebench V2.1 repaired wave, the sealed canonical)
The wave's oracle verdicts for three rows, compared against diagnostic runs of the SAME setup + gold patch + test command in the same environment family (the full captures linked below):

| instance | wave oracle reward | diagnostic run |
|---|---|---|
| blitz-js__superjson-78 | 0.0 | Test Suites: 8 passed, 8 total; Tests: 48 passed, 48 total |
| goplus__gop-1659 | 0.0 | 26 `ok` package markers, 0 `FAIL` |
| segmentio__encoding-45 | 0.0 | `--- PASS`, `PASS`, `ok` — 0 `FAIL` |

The suites are fully green; the recorded oracle rewards are 0.0.

### Suspected mechanism
The family config's test ids (FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS) are matched against the suite output by the taskcompendium log parser (parse_log_node for jest, the go-test parser for go). The parsed test names do not match the ids' form (the describe-block-qualified jest names vs the ids' form; the go package-level output), so the parse reports 0 matches and the reward collapses to 0.0.

### Reproduction
- The wave's ledger: s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/atlas/swe-repair/2026.11.20.1/wave-v11/fidelity-wave1-outcomes.json (the keys `<instance>|condensed|oracle`, reward 0.0).
- The diagnostic captures (the same setup + patch + test command, the full output): s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/atlas/swe-repair/2026.11.20.1/wave-v11/diagnose-blitz-js__superjson-78.txt (and the gop/encoding-45 siblings).

### Impact
The repair wave's oracle-failed tail (13,471 rows) includes a material share of such false negatives; the rows are graded 0.0 despite passing suites.

### Labels
agent-generated

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Fix landed on atlas-env-audit (f7d578fd5c), two parts:

1. **The capture-stream collision (the real cause):** the shared-source guest controller captured the original test.sh's stdout into the SAME `test_output.log` the source script's own `cat >` writes (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/shared_source.py`). Two writers at independent offsets cut the source's test-name lines mid-stream — the harness's own `test_cmd exit code:` echo glued into parsed names (`✓ creates a json file (18test_cmd exit code: 0`) and whole test lines lost at stomp boundaries. The capture stream now opens in **append mode**: the source's `cat` still owns and truncates its log; the harness's echo and grader output land after the source's content.

2. **The fail-closed parse repair (defense in depth):** the embedded grader removes the harness's own echo marker text, drops the duration fragment a cut interrupted, and flags the surviving name as truncated; the matcher resolves a truncated name only when exactly one configured id is consistent with the surviving prefix — any ambiguity stays unsatisfied.

Evidence: the DELTA5/DELTA6 zero-capture fixtures (17 corrupted parsed names, all in the all-pass-but-unresolved class); a same-log old-vs-new sweep over all 77 captures showed 0 broken matches and the recoveries predicted from the fixtures. Regression tests: the fixture-driven grader tests (`test_swe_rebench_v2_repair.py`) and the append-after-truncate ordering test (`test_root_delivery_contract.py`).

Effect on the rows in this issue's evidence: the corrupted-name rows re-admitted on the delta re-run (17/39 of the affected class so far, oracle reward 1.0); the remaining rows' dispositions are tracked in the repair lane.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
Launching several jobs that depend on the same uncached steps can fail one or more of them while checking a step's cache. On 2026-11-25, four Muse Glimmer eval jobs submitted within a minute of each other to cw-rno2a all built the same corpus and environment-image steps. Three failed, each on a different shared step:

```
s3fs.utils.FileExpired: [Errno 16] The remote file corresponding to filename
marin-us-east-08a/marin/data/eval/evalchemy-humanevalplus-1b269fdacec9ae28/2026.11.08.1/.executor_info
and Etag "b577a9cbcda68fc5563f773317429074" no longer exists.
```

The read is `StepRunner._launch_step` → `check_drift` → `read_record` → `_read_text` ([artifact.py:231](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L231)). s3fs records the object's ETag when it opens the file and fails if the object is replaced before the ranged read. Another job is evidently rewriting `.executor_info` between those two calls. The failed steps were `data/eval/evalchemy-humanevalplus-…`, `data/eval/harbor-bfcl-parity-1.0-pi-…` and `images/env-f25fb7e6001aef22`. The fourth job and the relaunched ones succeeded once the steps were cached.

Reproduce:
1. Choose eval selections whose corpus steps are not yet cached.
2. Submit several eval jobs that depend on them at the same moment, for example `experiments.evaluation.policy.cli launch --all-candidates`.

Expected: a job that finds a shared step being built by another job waits for it or reads it again, rather than failing.

`--all-candidates` submits one job per candidate at once, so a cold cache makes this likely for policy launches.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`check_drift()` reads the legacy `.executor_info` fallback when `.artifact.json` is absent, even for a step with no `SUCCESS` status. Concurrent cold-cache launchers can replace that schedule-time sidecar during the read, causing the reported `FileExpired` before the distributed lock is reached. No open PR addresses #12354.

**Relevant code**
- [`artifact.py#L286-L302`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L286-L302) — legacy sidecar fallback.
- [`step_runner.py#L352-L383`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L352-L383) — launcher reads before status.
- [`step_runner.py#L435-L451`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L435-L451) — worker repeats the read.

# Proposed Fix

Check status before reading drift metadata in the launcher, worker, and pruned-cache path. Read the record only for a successful cache entry, while still rebuilding mutable versions; cover the cold-cache case with an incomplete sidecar regression test.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 Fix: #12355 checks `SUCCESS` before reading drift metadata, so cold launches do not read a concurrently rewritten `.executor_info`. The new regression test and 132 execution tests pass; full pre-commit and advisory lint review pass.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
SWE-bench Multilingual's curated eval (#11676) runs its agents with internet access, because the Harbor packages it lowers don't set `allow_internet`. In the 100-task panel runs, agents used it to fetch the upstream repository and read the merged fix before passing, on `sharkdp__bat-3108` and `jqlang__jq-2750`. Other runs tried package registries and GitHub without passing. Local git history is not a leak: in every attempt that listed the full history, the newest commit was the task's base commit.

The effect grows with stronger models. On SWE-bench Multilingual, [Cursor](https://cursor.com/blog/reward-hacking-coding-benchmarks) measured 9.1 points between its standard and restricted harnesses for Opus 4.8 Max, and an [NVIDIA audit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06780) found that turning off the network lowered pass@1 by 9 to 13 points for three open models, almost all of it upstream retrieval. [Inspect's SWE-bench](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/coding/swe_bench) defaults to no internet.

The agent can't simply go offline, because each package's `test.sh` downloads its log parser with `uv` while grading, and grading runs in the agent's container. The fix runs the agent offline and grades it in Harbor's [separate verifier](https://docs.harborframework.com/news/separate-verifier-sandboxes): a fresh machine from the same image, with the network, that applies a patch of the agent's workspace taken after the agent stops. Upstream SWE-bench grades the same way, from a patch applied to a fresh container. It also keeps the agent away from the environment its tests run in.

Validation on Daytona, with the harness's hosted-model smoke loop:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Null agent (1 s), all 100 tasks | 99 graded 0 with an empty patch; every grader installed its parser over the network. 1 Daytona build failure, below |
| Hosted model, Terminus 2, 27 tasks, 15 min cap | 26 graded, 13 passed; no agent command reached the network, including on `bat-3108` and `jq-2750` (both 0) |
| `preact-2896` and `prometheus-13845`, 3 trials each | All 6 graded; patches 0.7 to 22 KB |

The smoke runs found three problems, fixed on the branch. Terminus 2 installs `tmux` at startup, so the offline images now install it at build time. One `preact` patch was killed while applying, most likely because it carried a large file such as a core dump, which Daytona sandboxes write into the working directory without a size limit; new files over 1 MiB now stay out of the patch, and a patch that fails to apply records an infrastructure error instead of a zero. `prometheus-13845`'s declarative build failed with "Image processing cancelled" on every retry in two runs, then built after a standalone build of the same Dockerfile, which suggests Daytona cached a cancelled build.

The packages now differ from the published Harbor ones in where they grade, not in what they grade. The version bump starts fresh corpora and records, so the panel needs to be rerun; Pi's option (local branch) will pick up the same setup.

It is draft and depends on [PR #12365](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12365). I found no separate fix to open; follow progress on those PRs.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The converted cohort graders (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/harbor_cohort_conversion.py`) run the verifier on the agent's machine as root and read the reward from artifacts copied off it. `7db57f9d39` hardened this: the collect sequence now kills leftover agent processes before the verifier runs and before the artifacts copy (Daytona provides no confirmed scoped descendant teardown, so an agent process that outlived its command could rewrite the reward file during the copy), and the reward path recomputes the verdict from the copied eval output, scoring zero on disagreement with the copied reward file.

The recomputation is per-family opt-in. Only the OpenSWE profile ships a verified rule (its fail-closed `OPENSWE_EXIT_CODE` marker contract over the copied eval output). The other fallback families keep the plain copy:

* swe-gym / swegym-validated: the reward derives from `/logs/verifier/native-output.txt` via an in-image adapter (`/opt/swegym-grader/bin/python /tests/native-adapter.py grade`). The adapter's own output joins `test-stdout.txt`, so the copied stdout is not byte-identical to the derivation input; the rule needs the derivation input copied separately or the re-run semantics verified.
* r2egym-patched: the derivation input `/logs/test_output.log` is not among the copied artifacts at all; `test_state.py` grades from it on the task machine.

Residual boundary, recorded deliberately: a root process racing the artifact copy on the same machine defeats any file-based integrity check, and the kill sweep is best effort (a process naming itself `daytona`, `toolbox` or `shellbox` survives by cmdline identity). The `SharedIntegrityContract`'s UID separation (agent 10001 / grader 10002) remains the stronger isolation for new SHARED SWE packages.

Done when:

* Each fallback family's recomputation rule lands with a divergence regression test (a planted reward that disagrees scores zero), or the family records why no rule is derivable from copied bytes.
* The r2egym derivation input joins the copied artifacts so its rule becomes derivable.
* The kill sweep's service-exclusion list stays validated against the live Daytona sandbox layout (planted writer dies; agent/toolbox and file round-trips survive).

issues.author: WhenWen
issues.body:
Opened on behalf of @WhenWen for the belay-wn research loop. Updates are posted here as results land.

**Question.** Why does MuonH (fixed-norm hyperball matrices) trail MuonW on KMA d768 fast_track? Can a weight-normalized optimizer beat a *fairly tuned* MuonW-family baseline? The work covers KMA d768 and the Belay ladder recipe (d512–d1280, plus the 8-minute d512 speedrun). All numbers are Paloma macro loss, and gaps under the 0.005 band count as ties.

**Current answer (2026-11-19).** With equal tuning, the weight-normalized forms tie tuned MuonC. Neither family leads anywhere.
- *Baseline.* The bar is MuonC (Defazio, arXiv 2506.02285): MuonW with matrix decay λ·lr_t/lr_max and an AdamW head. Its decay is tuned per length: best λ is 0.2–0.4 on the speedrun, 0.2 at ladder d512, and about 0.1 at d768. Both families also use the same s(t)² head anneal and late matrix anneal ("tl-d schedule").
- *Speedrun, d512, 8 min.* nonsi (learned per-matrix radius on MuonH) + schedule, with its starting size tuned, against tuned MuonC + schedule: +0.0007 over nine held-out seeds (95% −0.0033 to +0.0046). Both beat the recipe's MuonH by about 0.011–0.016.
- *Ladder d512.* nonsi + schedule against MuonC (λ 0.2) + schedule: +0.0033 on fresh seeds 4–7, a tie.
- *Formula-cap ball.* A no-decay ball whose per-layer cap comes from a shape/LR law, with no retuning. It ties MuonC + schedule on all four rungs: −0.0031, −0.0011, +0.0048 and −0.0029, one seed each. It also ties on the speedrun (+0.0004 over six seeds).
- *Mechanism.* Loss is set first by rotation per step and second by how matrix size evolves, not by where size ends up. A fit on MuonC's settings alone predicts nonsi's loss from its rotation to within 0.002. The original MuonH–MuonW gap fits the same picture: MuonH's rotation and size were off the optimum.
- *Open: d1280.* softcap + schedule (tl-d) trails MuonC + schedule by 0.0158 on one seed. Running d1024 width on d1280's recipe does not reproduce this, and a second seed is running.

**Intake posts.** speedrun-track proposals for nonsi + schedule (#9514, comment 7019355085) and MuonC (λ 0.2) + schedule (#9514, comment 7019433555).

**Running now**
- An "unnormalized hyperball" baseline: MuonH's norm-relative step with no projection, plus MuonC- or MuonW-style decay. It is tuned like MuonC and becomes the bar wherever it wins.
- MuonC decay brackets at d768–d1280.
- nonsi + schedule at d768–d1280, with seed 2.
- A second d1280 seed for tl-d vs MuonC + schedule.

Runs log to W&B project `understanding-sam/research-loop-belay-wn`.

comments.author: WhenWen
comments.body:
🤖 **Experiment log, part 1 of 3: the KMA d768 gap and the first weight-normalized fixes (2026-11-17)**

Setup: KMA d768 fast_track, batch 128, ctx 4096, 6,930 updates, 8×H100. Metric: final validation loss on the tuning split (plus a fixed held-out set once it was verified). Seeds are paired.

**Baselines reproduced**
- MuonW seeds 0/1/3: 2.51555 / 2.51564 / 2.5219 (four-seed mean 2.5182).
- MuonH seeds 0/1/2: 2.52054 / 2.52530 / 2.52428.
- Mean paired gap +0.0057 (+0.0064 over three paired seeds). On the fixed held-out set it is +0.0054, lower bound > 0.
- MuonW LR ×0.71 / ×1.41 is worse than ×1.
- Checkpoint restore is bitwise exact on H100, and interrupted-vs-uninterrupted continuation matches.

**Where the gap is** (log reads and swap runs)
- MuonH's deficit is front-loaded: +1.8 nats in the first 100 steps, about 0 by step 5000, then a ~0.006 loss in the final anneal.
- Swaps put the whole gap in the hidden-matrix update:
  - MuonW matrices + MuonH head/Adam groups: 2.5164.
  - MuonH matrices + MuonW Adam groups: 2.5218.
  - Gates and fallbacks don't matter.
- Rotation vs size, finals:
  - ShadowH (MuonW's rotation on fixed spheres) ends at MuonH's level: best 2.5273, ×0.5 2.5360, ×2 2.5441.
  - MuonH's rotation with MuonW's size law ends at 2.5112 / 2.5138.
  - So the gap is weight scale, not rotation.
- MuonW for the first 1,000 steps, then MuonH holding those sizes: 2.5078. MuonH's problem is mainly its first ~1,000 steps at the small init size.

**Candidates (MuonH step + some way to set the matrix size)**
- *Fixed bigger spheres* at 0.66× the update size: 2.5178 (seed 0), equal to MuonW's mean.
- *C2* (radius follows MuonW's size law in closed form): 2.5112 / 2.5138 on seeds 0–1. On held-out it is −0.006 / −0.003 vs MuonW.
- *C3* (grow by that law for 1,000 steps, then hold) on seeds 1–5:
  - −0.0057 vs original MuonW.
  - −0.0024 vs tuned MuonW (not claimed).
- *Radial MuonH* (learned log-radius per slice, Adam on ⟨G, W⟩):
  - 2.5047 / 2.5082 on seeds 0–1, about 0.01 below MuonW.
  - But radii ran away up to ~4,600× on slices whose output feeds a norm. Their radial gradient is rounding noise, and Adam with ε≈0 turns it into full steps.

🤖 **Experiment log, part 3 of 3: new weight-normalized forms, the mechanism, and what is running (2026-11-18 → 11-19)**

**Forms that did not beat MuonC (KMA d768, two seeds, same commit unless noted)**
- *Weight-normalized MuonC* (radius follows MuonC's decay law): 2.5121 / 2.5148, which is +0.011 vs MuonC. Changing decay moved the size 5× but the loss only ≤ 0.004.
- *ShadowC* (MuonC's rotation on a sphere): 2.5189 at init radius. With softcap's learned radius it gets 2.5086 (λ0.1), still worse than plain softcap.
- *Learned gain on MuonC* (MuonW family): adds nothing (+0.0007 to +0.0034). A weight-normalized head on MuonC's matrices costs about 0.
- *Four new constraint shapes, all with interior LR brackets:*
  - spectral-norm sphere: 2.4994, ties tl-d, −0.0018 behind MuonC + schedule
  - capped ball: +0.0020 vs tl-d
  - per-row radii: +0.0030 vs tl-d
  - Stiefel/orthogonal: about 0.10 worse; the constraint was verified exact, so this is real
- *Per-family caps* on the formula-cap ball: no gain (−0.0008 to +0.0092). *Caps at a fixed multiple of init:* best +0.003 vs the law cap.

**Forms that tie MuonC**
- *Formula-cap ball* (no decay; per-layer cap = 0.71·√(39·lr_max/(2·0.1))·|U_l|):
  - KMA d768: 2.4978 vs MuonC + schedule 2.4967.
  - Belay ladder vs same-commit MuonC (λ0.1) + schedule: −0.0031 / −0.0011 / +0.0048 / −0.0029 (d512–d1280).
  - Speedrun: +0.0004 over six seeds vs MuonC λ0.4.
  - It beats tl-d by 0.018 at d1280.
- *Ball capped at MuonC's measured final sizes* (explanation only): 2.49695 vs 2.49694.

**Mechanism, measured**
- Rotation per step is the first variable. Across MuonC and nonsi settings it explains loss with R² 0.97 on the ladder; final matrix size explains 0.02. A fit on MuonC's settings alone predicts nonsi's loss to within 0.002.
- Size is second, and it is the path over training that matters, not the end point:
  - Pinning nonsi at MuonC's final per-layer sizes loses ~0.009.
  - nonsi at start ×4 ends at MuonC's size with the same rotation and is 0.008 worse.
- In this recipe MuonC's matrices grow toward a fixed per-layer size and hold, without shrinking late.
- The formula-cap ball behaves like MuonC at about 1.2× its nominal decay, which is why its larger cap ties and its smaller cap loses.
- tl-d's d1280 loss is not radius stranding; tl-d's radii there are larger than softcap's. d1024 width on d1280's recipe does not reproduce it: nonsi + schedule and MuonC + schedule both score 2.3478 there.
- The original KMA H–W gap fits the same picture: MuonH's rotation and its size path were away from the optimum early on.

**Running now**
- *Unnormalized hyperball (uhs).* MuonH's step relative to the current norm (MuonH's tuned angular step, no projection), plus MuonC- or MuonW-style decay, with MuonC's AdamW head (0.35×, s² anneal in the schedule cells). Decay is bracketed per rung around its own balance point. Speedrun first, then the ladder. It replaces MuonC as a rung's bar if it wins.
- *MuonC decay brackets:* λ0.05 at d768; λ0.2 at d1024/d1280, run as H100 and GB200 sets.
- *nonsi + schedule:* d1024/d1280, seed 2, and d1280 head-only / anneal-only splits.
- *d1280 seed 2* for tl-d vs MuonC + schedule.
- *Formula-cap ball:* no-schedule pair at d1280.

All comparisons are now scored on the same hardware type. A difference between hardware types is only allowed as a difference of same-hardware differences.

**Goal change.** The target is now a weight-normalized optimizer that *beats* tuned MuonC + the s² anneals; a tie no longer counts. New lines should be designs derived from the measured mechanism, not new grids on existing forms (tuning only as much as a fair comparison needs).

- **Train-vs-Paloma offset (tdg, 308 speedrun runs, 260 pairs):** weight-normalized forms trail MuonC 0.005–0.008 more on training loss than on Paloma. It is a head trait, not a cost of weight normalization, and no held-out gain is hidden behind it.
- **Momentum echo (derivation, then a check):** each Muon update points back along its own recent steps through momentum, so ⟨Ô, Ŵ⟩ ≈ −κθ with κ ≈ 10.7. This accounts for the radial drift of the unnormalized hyperball and for the KDA w_beta runaway. It predicted the d512-ladder neutral decay at 0.152; the smoke run measured 0.166.
- **Direction noise (KMA d768):** about 80% of each Muon step goes along the momentum's noise-like directions, which hold only ~20% of its energy.

comments.body:

**Why the forms tie, and what is next.** The planner wrote out the premises behind the weight-normalized ≈ MuonC equivalence:
1. Muon's near-constant step size.
2. A Frobenius-norm constraint that decay relaxes.
3. Slowly varying per-slice rules that MuonC copies by scaling LR and decay together.
4. A fixed norm target.
5. A free weight spectrum.

Two new designs break premises no earlier line broke:
- **A Schatten-4 ball** caps runaway top singular values and leaves the rest of the spectrum and Muon's step alone. No scalar decay can express it. It is tested at the speedrun against tuned MuonC, the Frobenius law ball, and MuonC given matching Schatten-4 shrinkage.

Per-row spheres were not run: row-normalized MuonC is their exact decay twin, so they can only tie. Earlier KMA runs already covered Stiefel (+0.106), the spectral sphere (+0.0018) and per-row radii (+0.0046).

issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Add loop guards for agent traces at four layers: SFT data filters, wait demonstrations, an episode stop on stalls, and a loop metric in evals. Then test the RL and decoding guards Marin already has. The design follows IFM's [`repetition_check.py`](https://github.com/ifm-ai/process_entry/blob/main/repetition_check.py) and the K2-Horizon results ([arXiv 2611.21003](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.21003v1)). The full survey of Marin's current loop guards, with citations, is [here](https://gistpreview.github.io/?3d44de572b8babfc08f96ac90a05b109).

## Background

- **SFT filter (main).** The only agent-loop filter is `has_stalled_tool_call` in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py`, added in #9259. It drops a record on the third identical tool call after two identical replies, within one user turn, and fired on 101 of 210,031 sampled conversations.
  - It misses Terminus-2 traces, because terminal output is stored as user turns and each one resets the counter.
  - It misses spread-out repetition.
- **Ending episodes (missing).** Nothing ends an episode when the agent repeats itself. The rolloutengine stops only at turn, token or time limits. Terminus-2's `turn_callback` can return EARLY_TERMINATION, but no callback uses it.
- **RL penalties (unused).** Vendored SkyRL has two loop penalties, both off by default. The loop-credit penalty was swept in #9599 and no strength stood out. No recipe enables the antithrash penalty for repeated actions.
- **Doom loops (in flight).** #9691 and #12240 target repeated token suffixes at the end of a response. They don't cover repeated actions, and `loop_audit.py` lives only on branch `benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo`.
- **Evals (no metric).** There is no standing loop metric. #7743 measured median exact-duplicate tool-call fractions of 20–37%, but only once.
- **IFM's evidence.**
  - RL cut exact repeats inside Terminal-Bench interrupt loops from 61.8% to 0.3%. Trials with a loop barely changed, from 12.9% to 11.6%.
  - SFT demonstrations of waiting after unchanged output brought interrupt loops below 1%. In IFM's midtraining data, the agent waited 0 times out of 446 such moments.

## Proposed work

1. **IFM-style rules in `chat_normalize.py`.**
   - Reject 8 consecutive identical name+args tool calls, whatever the replies.
   - Reject a call that occurs at least 10 times, accounts for at least 30% of assistant turns, and appears in a run of at least 3 identical calls.
   - For Terminus-2 records, reject at least 8 consecutive identical normalized assistant messages when one preceding observation accounts for at least 80% of the run.
   - Keep #9259's exemption for retries that get a different reply.
   - Report fire rates per source, and hand-check a sample for precision.
2. **Wait demonstrations.**
   - Audit the SFT and midtraining mixes for what the agent does after unchanged terminal output.
   - Add Terminus-2 rows that wait or poll on long-running commands, next to the recovery rows from #10888.
   - Generate them in a real-clock environment, because ShellSim sleeps take no wall time (#10159).
3. **Stall stop in the rolloutengine.**
   - Add a stop reason such as `REPEAT_STALL` that fires after 3 consecutive identical action batches with identical observations.
   - Grade the task anyway, so work done before the stall still earns credit.
   - Add it to the #12190 port list, and either confirm or remove the "thrashing detector" that the #6341 checklist marks done.
4. **Loop metrics in evals.**
   - Merge `loop_audit.py` to main.
   - Add to the #10197 eval policy: loop count and upper bound, the exact-duplicate tool-call fraction (the #7743 method), and an interrupt-loop count on Terminal-Bench.
   - Report repeats inside loops and the share of trials with a loop separately.
5. **Antithrash ablation.**
   - Enable `antithrash` on one agentic RL recipe.
   - Add an option to apply it only to otherwise-correct trajectories.
   - Track both measures from item 4.
6. **Decoding checks.**
   - Run a paired comparison of `repetition_penalty` 1.0 against 1.1 on the snowball-sft eval and the curriculum-RL policy.
   - Land #12254 with a full set of stop tokens.

## Done when

- [ ] `chat_normalize.py` has the three IFM-style rules with tests, and per-source fire rates are posted here.
- [ ] A wait-behaviour audit of the SFT and midtraining mixes is posted, and a wait-demonstration source is in the SFT mix.
- [ ] The rolloutengine records a repeat-stall stop reason, and the #6341 "thrashing detector" entry is confirmed or corrected.
- [ ] Eval reports show loop counts, the duplicate tool-call fraction, and the Terminal-Bench interrupt-loop share.
- [ ] Antithrash ablation results are posted with both loop measures.
- [ ] Results of the paired `repetition_penalty` test are posted, and #12254 has merged.

Related: #9259, #9599, #9691, #12240, #7743, #10197, #12190, #6341, #10888, #10159, #12254.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`has_stalled_tool_call` checks three identical calls with identical replies only within one user turn; the Terminus converter stores terminal observations as user messages, so that counter resets between shell steps. The native RolloutEngine records turns and stop reasons, then grades after the harness exits; it has no repeat-stall reason. [#12167](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12167) has merged, while [#12240](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12240) measures token suffix loops separately.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_normalize.py#L144-L174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L144-L174) — current within-turn rule
- [`download/terminus.py#L77-L123`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/terminus.py#L77-L123) — terminal output becomes user message
- [`recorder.py#L250-L318`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L250-L318) — transitions and observations
- [`engine.py#L216-L255`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L216-L255) — harness exit and grading
- [`agents/terminus/agent.py#L986-L1012`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/agents/terminus/agent.py#L986-L1012) — command observation loop

# Proposed Fix

1. Define one action identity (tool name plus canonical arguments), observation identity, and Terminus message normalization against saved traces. Audit the three proposed thresholds in report-only mode across each SFT source. Publish source counts, sampled true/false positives, and the decision on how changed replies interact with the eight-call rule before filtering data.
2. Add the three filters at chat normalization, with separate counters and tests for user-message observations, nonadjacent repeats, changed replies, parallel batches, and final tool calls. Rebuild affected source artifacts only after the precision audit; link the filter PR `Part of #12264`.
3. Add a `repeat_stall` stop reason to RolloutEngine when three completed action batches and their observations match. End before the next model request and use the existing grading path so completed work keeps its score. Test changing observations, timeout precedence, and a scored stall without fabricated model turns; add the behavior to [#12190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12190) and verify the claim in [#6341](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6341).
4. Count what the agent does after unchanged terminal output in the pinned SFT and midtraining mixes. Add a real-clock Terminus wait/poll source beside [#10888](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10888)'s recovery rows, then publish source identity, row count, and a hand audit that the waits actually allow time to pass.
5. Port `loop_audit.py` from the [#12240 branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo) as a reviewed, reusable metric. Pin loop and duplicate-call denominators, report both repeats inside loops and trials with a loop, and add Terminal-Bench interrupt-loop counts to the eval report and [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197). Baseline these metrics before any training intervention.
6. With that baseline fixed, run one antithrash ablation (including the correct-trajectory-only variant) and paired `repetition_penalty` 1.0/1.1 evals on identical prompts and decoding budgets. Report task scores, loop measures, and sampling settings together. [#12254](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12254) is currently a finish-reason PR with an open turn-boundary stop-token review finding; resolve that finding and verify the full stop-token set before treating it as a decoding guard.

These are separate data, runtime, eval, and experiment changes. Each stage can land as a reviewable PR or published measurement without claiming the full issue is done.

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 **Marin Belay intake: post research ideas for [Marin Belay](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/) here.**

Marin Belay is a human-guided, agent-executed experiment loop that hill-climbs the grug `fast_track` scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss).

**Start with the [contributor guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin_belay_v1_recipe/experiments/belay/CONTRIBUTING.md)**: how to check an idea against the recipe, pick a Track, follow its runs, and take it up the ladder.

1. **Post one idea per comment**, with a paper link or a short rationale. One idea is one change judged against one control; several values of one setting (up to 4) count as one. Post combinations of changes as separate ideas, and a follow-up step (such as tuning the winner) as a new comment once the first result is in. Add a `Track:` line to pick the baseline; the default is `speedrun` (the 8-minute d512 run). The Belay page lists the Tracks.
2. **A maintainer reviews it** on the Belay admin page and approves it for an agent session, or declines it with a reason.
3. **👀 on your comment means it has been reviewed.** Nothing else is posted here. Plans, results and decline reasons are on the Status page.

**The usual path for an idea:** optionally a `vanilla-*` Track first, for a radical idea or a stronger signal; then `speedrun`, for fast iteration and to check it fits the current recipe; then `hero-mfu` if it will change MFU a lot; then `ladder`. Maintainers promote ideas into the recipe from those results.

**Tracks** (the `Track:` line):

| Track | Runs against | Hardware |
|---|---|---|
| `speedrun` (default) | The 8-minute d512 run of the current recipe; judged at equal data, then equal time if the step time changes | 1× 8×H100 |
| `competitive-d512` … `competitive-d1280` | The current recipe at one ladder rung, compared with its finished baseline run | 8×H100; d1280 on 4 nodes |
| `ladder` | All four `competitive-*` rungs at once, at the baseline's step count. After a `hero-mfu` result, each rung's steps are adjusted for the MFU change (better MFU, more steps). Without one, the verdict is provisional: the idea needs a `hero-mfu` result before it joins the recipe | as above |
| `moe-d512` … `moe-d1280` | A basic MoE at that rung | 8×H100 |
| `vanilla-d512` … `vanilla-d1280` | A dense baseline at that rung | 8×H100 |
| `hero-mfu` | Step time of the hero GB200 stack; a maintainer runs it | 1 GB200 rack |
| `custom` | A study: runs on other Tracks, then an analysis report with no win/loss verdict; needs a node and hours budget | per study |

Wins are judged on Paloma macro loss with a noise band of 0.005 (`hero-mfu`: step time, ±0.5%).

**Example comments**

> Try warming the MuonH momentum up from 0.85 to 0.98 over the first 10% of training, as modded-nanogpt does.

> Track: moe-d768
> Replace the router's sigmoid combine weights with softmax over the top-8 experts.

> Track: ladder
> Take X0221 (CPLM Plus) up the ladder with the settings of its speedrun win.

> Track: custom
> Measure how the stable rank of each attention projection changes over a full d512 run, from checkpoints every 1,000 steps.

**The Belay app** ([public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-…](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/)):

- **[Belay](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/):** the project. It covers the current recipe, the scaling ladder and its projection, the timeline, the gates an idea passes, the Tracks, the data and the starter kit.
- **[Status](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/#status):** every idea and its results across the gates (Dense, speedrun, Hero MFU, projection, recipe), live runs and queue, and the agent log with one thread per idea (`#status/X####`).
- **[Hero MFU](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/#mfu):** hero-scale throughput, with each MFU change on the GB200 stack and its branch.
- **[Admin](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/#admin)** (maintainers, signed in to Marina): review and approve or decline ideas, with instructions and node, hours and priority grants. It also sets the node cap, dispatch and GitHub reactions.

Notice: The majority of our compute right now is dedicated to SFT and RL runs. As a result, runs outside the speedrun track may queue up for a couple days.
